titre: Opening a Livret A or Livret jeune savings account for my child
resume: Which savings account to choose, what documents to bring to the bank (for the child and each parent), the ceilings, who can withdraw depending on age, and what changes if you are separated.
aQuoiCaSert: A savings account in the child's name lets you put money aside for them, with no fees and tax-free interest. The Livret A (a regulated, tax-free savings account) can be opened from birth, the Livret jeune (a youth savings account) from age 12. The money belongs to the child: parents manage it on the child's behalf and may only use it for expenses directly related to the child (education, upkeep). From age 16, parents must account to the child for how the money was used.
quiEstConcerne: Parents (or a guardian) who want to save for their child, from birth for the Livret A.
Young people aged 12 to 25 who usually live in France, for the Livret jeune.
Grandparents or relatives who want to give money: they can pay into the account, but it must be opened by the child or the child's legal representative.
aSavoir: Livret A: only one per person, ceiling of €22,950 (excluding interest), minimum deposit of €10 (€1.50 at La Banque Postale). Interest rate of 1.7% from August 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027.

Livret jeune: only one per person, from 12 to 25, deposit ceiling of €1,600, rate set by the bank but never lower than the Livret A rate, opened with at least €10. For a minor, the bank requires the legal representative's signature.
Withdrawals before 16: the child cannot withdraw without the legal representative's consent. On the Livret A, the legal representative can only withdraw at the branch where the account was opened.
Withdrawals from 16 to 18: the young person can withdraw alone from their Livret A or Livret jeune, unless a legal representative objects by registered letter sent to the bank.

Parents who share parental authority (even if separated): everyday acts can be done by one parent, but the Cour de cassation (France's highest court) ruled on June 12, 2025 that a transaction that changes a minor's account, such as an outgoing transfer, requires both parents' consent. The bank may therefore ask for both signatures.
If only one parent holds parental authority (judgment or special situation), that parent acts alone: bring the decision that proves it.

documents.libelle: The child's ID or, failing that, the family record book (livret de famille)
documents.detail: Original. Also serves as proof of date of birth, required for the Livret jeune. No ID card? See the guide entry "Getting my child's ID card or passport".
Original plus a copy of the parents' and child's pages. It proves parentage. Failing that, the child's full birth certificate showing parentage (free on service-public.gouv.fr).

documents.libelle: Valid ID of the parent signing
documents.detail: Original. If the bank requires both parents' signatures, also bring the other parent's ID or arrange for them to come.
Bill, tax notice or rent receipt in the parent's name. Many banks ask for one less than 3 months old: check.

documents.libelle: Judgment or decision on parental authority, if you hold it alone
documents.detail: Copy of the judgment of the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF) or of the decision giving you sole parental authority.

documents.libelle: Written consent of the other parent, if the bank asks for it
documents.detail: Dated and signed letter, with a copy of their ID. Essential for large withdrawals or transfers if you share parental authority.
At least €10 (€1.50 for a Livret A at La Banque Postale).

documents.libelle: Account opening contract and annual statements
documents.detail: Keep them: they prove the amounts paid in and withdrawn.

etapes.detail: Livret A from birth, Livret jeune from age 12. The child can have both. Check that no Livret A has already been opened in the child's name (for example by a grandparent): only one per person.

etapes.titre: Talk it over with the other parent
etapes.detail: Agree on the account, the bank and who will make deposits. A written agreement avoids blockages when it comes to withdrawals.

etapes.titre: Make an appointment at your chosen bank
etapes.detail: Ask for the exact list of documents: it can vary from bank to bank, especially on whether both parents must be present or sign.

Child's valid ID or family record book, original family record book, your valid ID, recent proof of address, judgment if you hold parental authority alone, the other parent's signed consent and ID if the bank requires it, money for the first deposit.

etapes.titre: Sign the account opening at the bank
etapes.detail: The parent signs on behalf of the child. For the Livret jeune, the legal representative's signature is required.

etapes.titre: File the contract and follow the statements
etapes.detail: Store the contract and each annual statement in the Vault. Note the key milestones: age 12, age 16 (withdrawals alone), age 18.

ou.nom: The bank of your choice or La Banque Postale
ou.detail: The Livret A and the Livret jeune are offered by most banks. Compare the Livret jeune terms, as its rate varies from bank to bank.

aConfirmer: The exact documents, and whether both parents must be present or sign, are set by each bank: ask for the list before your appointment.
Official sources do not set a minimum age for a minor to open a Livret A alone: your bank may have its own rules.
